title: Mapping Window+V to  any other key when use at background  unlike the usual fixed popup menu  doesn't automatically paste when clicking

status.label: Reproduce the remapped clipboard-history behavior
status.detail: A commenter reports reproducing the behavior on PowerToys 0.100.2 and Windows 11 25H2. The mapping direction is Alt+C to Win+V; the component responsible is not yet established.

judgment.rationale: The original report describes an Alt+C-to-Win+V remap whose clipboard popup behaves differently outside the Keyboard Manager settings window. A commenter explicitly reports reproducing the behavior on PowerToys 0.100.2 and Windows 11 25H2, and clarifies the mapping direction. That supports maintainer reproduction, but the comment also suspects Windows clipboard behavior, so the responsible component is not established well enough for a fix design.
evidence: The issue body lists PowerToys 0.88 and says the behavior differs when the remapped shortcut is used outside the foreground Remap Shortcut settings interface.
The body describes mapping Alt+C to Win+V; the commenter explicitly clarifies this direction.
The commenter reports reproducing the behavior with PowerToys 0.100.2 on Windows 11 25H2.
The commenter suspects a Windows issue, so the current evidence does not isolate Keyboard Manager as the cause.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the numbered sequence on current stable and compare the remapped shortcut with native Win+V before assigning the failure to Keyboard Manager or proposing a code change.

fix_assessment.rationale: A current-version reproduction is reported, but the available evidence does not distinguish a Keyboard Manager defect from Windows clipboard-history behavior. Establish the failing component through the focused reproduction before proposing an implementation change.

actions.label: Reproduce clipboard history with the saved remap
actions.note: The issue has a reported current-version reproduction; compare native Win+V and the saved remap before requesting more diagnostics.

reproduce.title: Compare native Win+V with an Alt+C remap
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.100.2 or current stable on Windows 11 25H2
prerequisites: Use an application with a text field that accepts pasted text.
setup: In Keyboard Manager, save a shortcut mapping from Alt+C to Win+V.
steps: Copy at least two distinct text entries so Clipboard History has selectable items.
Focus the target application's text field and press native Win+V; record when the history popup appears and what happens after clicking an item.
Repeat with the saved Alt+C mapping while the target application remains in the foreground.
Repeat the remapped shortcut with the Remap Shortcut settings interface foreground, as described in the report, and compare the results.
reproduce.expected_result: The saved Alt+C mapping should invoke Clipboard History like native Win+V, and selecting an item should paste it into the focused application's text field. Any difference between the foreground-settings and background-app cases should be recorded.
